rules.rule: Never force-push a shared branch; rebase locally and push a new branch instead.
Stage files by name before committing so unrelated edits stay out of the commit.
Run pytest with --basetemp under the session scratch directory, not /tmp.
When a CI job fails on a known flaky test, rebase onto the newest main and push again rather than waiting.
Run the test suite with the worktree's own virtualenv interpreter, never the global python shim.
In Slack messages write links as bare URLs, because markdown link syntax renders literally.
Post follow-ups to a report as replies in the same Slack thread, not as new channel messages.
Request ReadOnly credentials for any AWS call that only lists or describes resources.
Assert the AWS account id with get-caller-identity before every batch of calls.
Close the SQLite connection before deleting its temporary directory, or Windows refuses the delete.
Show every time to the user in Pacific Time, never in UTC.
In Java keep explicit types instead of var, even when a reviewer suggests var.
Fix review findings in the pending draft revision rather than opening a new code review revision.
Bracket the first letter of a pgrep pattern so the search cannot match its own shell.
rules.negative: Never pkill a pattern that also appears in the invoking command line.

rules.rule: Exclude PNG files from git diff --check so raw image bytes never print into the terminal.
Do not run docker system prune on a shared build host; remove only the images you created.
Pause the Kafka consumer group before resetting its offsets.
Run terraform plan and read the diff before any terraform apply on a production workspace.
Lower the DNS record TTL a day before migrating a hostname to a new load balancer.
Give a scheduled script that calls a slow network API an explicit timeout above two minutes.
Redact tokens and session cookies from logs before attaching them to a ticket.
Ship risky changes behind a feature flag that defaults off, and enable it per region.
Write every schema migration so it can run twice without error.
Create database indexes concurrently on large tables so writes are not blocked.
Page through list APIs with the continuation token instead of assuming one response holds every item.
Retry throttled API calls with exponential backoff and jitter, capped at five attempts.
Write commit subjects in plain words without a conventional prefix like feat or fix.
Use no em dashes in prose written for people; use a full stop instead.
Start a new direct message with Hi followed by the person's first name.
When booking a meeting room, add the room's address to the calendar invite to reserve it.
Take browser screenshots without a filename argument so they cannot overwrite a file in the repository.
Bind any local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1 explicitly, never to all interfaces.
Write credentials to disk with umask 077 and report only the file mode, never the value.
Run npm ci after rebasing across a dependency upgrade before trusting a failing frontend gate.
Prove a new test catches the bug by reverting the fix and watching the test fail.
Report a failure rate with its denominator, never a bare failure count.
Never conclude a value is absent from output that was cut off with head.
A bounded queue's put_nowait discards the newest item when full; evict the oldest explicitly if that is the policy.
Invalidate the CDN cache path after replacing a static asset with the same filename.
Forward the SSH agent only to hosts you control, never to a shared jump box.
